By the present writ petition the petitioner has called in question the proceedings dated 20.12.2018 titled as endorsement issued by the 3rd respondent, pursuant to the order of this Court dated 31.08.2018 in WP.No.22125 of 2018, whereby the representations submitted by the petitioner dated 18.09.2017, 19.12.2017 and 24.07.2018 ventilating his grievance has been considered and rejected.

The petitioner had sought for quashing the said proceeding with a consequential direction to the respondents to regularise the petitioner's period of suspension and non- employment and to promote him as Police Constable Grade-I w.e.f. 09.03.2003 and as Head Constable w.e.f.
09.06.2008 and as Special Sub Inspector w.e.f. 01.06.2018 with all consequential monetary benefits.

2. Heard the learned counsel for the petitioner and the learned Special Government Pleader appearing on behalf of the respondents and perused the record.

Briefly stated the case of the petitioner is that he had joined the service as Police Constable Grade II on 09.06.1993; that on 11.09.1995, alleging that he had unnecessarily quarrelled with staff working in Valluvar Kottam and his subsequent involvement in Cr.No.1424 of 1995 on the file of the Nungambakkam Police Station was placed under suspension till 08.12.1996, and that thereafter he was visited with punishment of removal from service vide Proceedings dated 09.06.1999.
4.

It is the further case of the petitioner, that aggrieved by the order of punishment of removal from service, he had preferred an appeal to the Deputy Inspector General of Police, Armed Police; that the said authority by an order dated 21.08.1999 held that pending trial in Cr.No.1424 of 1995, it is illegal to pass order removing from service and revoked the order removing him from service, stating that the final orders will be passed after the disposal of the criminal case by the trial Court and allowed him to join duty .
5.

The petitioner further contended that the FIR registered against him vide Cr.No.1424 of 1995, on charge sheet being filed by the concerned police authority was assigned SC.No.721 of 2004, and the trial Court had https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis ( Uploaded on: 07/11/2025 07:48:40 pm )
acquitted him of all the charges vide order dated 08.04.2005; that as the earlier order of punishment of removal from service was set aside in appeal, observing that final orders will be passed after the disposal of the criminal case by the Trial Court, the Deputy Commissioner, Anna Nagar, Chennai by his order dated 06.03.2006 awarded punishment of reduction in time scale of pay by three stages for three years with cumulative effect.
6.

It is further case of the petitioner that aggrieved by the aforesaid order imposing penalty, he had preferred an appeal to the 2nd respondent herein; that the 2nd respondent by order dated S.Ramesh Babu vs The Director General Of Police on 7 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/29454605/
2 19.06.2006 modified the punishment as awarded, into punishment of postponement of increment for one year without cumulative effect; that the petitioner thereafter preferred a mercy petition to the 1st respondent requesting him to cancel the modified punishment; and that the 1st respondent by order dated 14.03.2011 modified the punishment imposed on him into one Black Mark.
7.

On behalf of the respondents it is contended that on the order of punishment of removal from service being set aside by the appellate authority observing that the proceedings can be initiated after the decision in the criminal proceedings, the petitioner was reinstated into service on 02.12.1999; that the period of suspension from 11.09.1995 to 08.12.1996 and the period when the petitioner was out of service on account of passing of the order of removal from service i.e. from 09.06.1999 to 01.12.1999, was treated as eligible leave with EOL to the extent necessary, by the 3rd respondent vide Proceedings dated 02.07.2017; that the total period of 376 days was treated as Leave Without Pay (in short LWP) due to non availability of eligible leave to the petitioner's leave account.

11. It is contended by the respondents that after deducting LWP, period from his total period of service on completion of 10 years of service as Grade II Constable, the petitioner was upgraded as Police Constable Grade I w.e.f. 23.06.2004 and thereafter to the position of Head Constable w.e.f.

On behalf of the respondents it is contended that the entire period of suspension was adjusted towards 30 days Earned Leave, 90 days Unearned Leave (PA) and 334 days as LWP and that insofar as out of employment period from 09.06.1999 to 01.12.1999 is concerned 44 days was adjusted towards Earned Leave, 90 days towards Unearned Leave (P) and 42 days as LWP.
13.

On behalf of the respondents, it is contended that since, the petitioner did not have sufficient leave to his credit, the suspension period and out of employment period beyond the adjustable leave period available, was considered as LWP; and that the said period of 376 days ie. in 334 days during suspension period and 42 days out of employment period, though is considered as leave, as the same is without pay, the same cannot be reckoned as petitioner being in service for being considered as qualifying service in order to be granted promotion to the post of Constable Grade I and Head Constable and thereafter being eligible for promotion to Special Sub Inspector.

18. I have taken note of the respective contentions urged.

19. The fulcrum of the petitioner's case is that on the order of removal from service being set aside and thereafter the petitioner being visited with penalty of reduction in time scale of pay by three stages for three years with cumulative effect and the said order of punishment being modified in appeal to postponement of increment for one year without cumulative effect and the said order further being modified to a punishment / recording of Black Mark in service register in a mercy petition filed by the petitioner herein, the period of suspension and out of service is to be regularised as per Rule 54 of Tamil Nadu Government Servant Fundamental Rules applicable to the Government servant; and that if the period of suspension and out of service is considered as being in duty, he would be eligible for upgradation as Grade I Constable on 09.06.2003, as Head Constable on 09.06.2008 and https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis ( Uploaded on: 07/11/2025 07:48:40 pm )
further being eligible to be upgraded as Special Sub Inspector on completion of 10 years from 10.06.2018.
20.

The petitioner claimed that on account of the order of punishment being set aside or modified,
to a mere Black Mark which is nothing but censure, the same cannot be treated as punishment,
and thus, the period of suspension and out of service is to be treated as on duty for all purposes, as provided under Rule 54 of Fundamental Rules.

21. It is to be noted that the modification of the punishment initially awarded (i.e,) reduction in time scale of pay by three stages for three years with cumulative effect, to finally one of the punishment of Black Mark by the first respondent vide his proceedings dated 14.03.2011, firstly, cannot be said as if the petitioner is not visited with any punishment and secondly, having been reinstated into service on the ground that the charges has not been proved against him or by giving benefit of doubt or any other technical ground, for him to claim the benefit under Rule 54 of the Fundamental Rules.
https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis

22. In police service, the recording of Black Mark is also considered as a kind of punishment and the same will reflect in the service record of the concerned individual and also have a bearing during S.Ramesh Babu vs The Director General Of Police on 7 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/29454605/
5 his tenure of service.

sentences.text: 23. Further, by the Police Standing Orders also the Black Mark is considered as punishment.

Thus the contention of the petitioner that the Black Mark being a form of censure, cannot be treated as punishment for him to claim the benefit under Rule 54 of the Fundamental Rules does not appeal to this Court for being accepted.

24. Insofar as the claim of including or counting the period of LWP in the period of service of the petitioner is concerned, answer to the said claim can be found in 'The Tamil Nadu Leave Rules,1993'
(for short Leave Rules).
The Rule 4 (a) of the Leave Rules provides as to what is considered as 'duty' and inclusions thereunder.
A reading of the said Rule https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis

(

25. The Apex Court in the case of Delhi Transport Corporation v. Balwan Singh and others reported in (2019) 18 SCC 126 dealing with qualifying service for pension had held that where for a leave sanctioned, leave salary is payable, that period can only be counted and if an employee is not paid for leave, that period has to be excluded from the period to be counted for admissibility of pension.
26.

sentences.text: It is also to be noted that the petitioner on being granted upgradation to Grade I Constable on 26.03.2004 did not raise any objection or submit any representation for not being granted the upgradation w.e.f. 09.06.2003 as claimed now.

27. Admittedly, the silence on the part of the petitioner at the relevant point of time was on account of pendency of criminal case vide SC.No.721 of 2004 which ended in acquittal order on 08.04.2005.

Further, the petitioner also did not raise any objection when he was granted further upgradation as Head constable on 23.06.2009 as against the claim of being eligible for upgradation to the said position on 09.06.2008.
The petitioner accepted both the upgradations (i.,e) Constable Grade I and Head Constable by excluding the period of LWP of 376 days by the respondents.
The petitioner also allowed the order of the first respondent by which the punishment was modified to 'Black Mark' to attain finality.

29. Further, it is also to be noted that even after the 1 st respondent modified the order of appellate authority to that of Black Mark vide order dated 14.03.2011 on the basis of mercy petition filed by him, the petitioner not only did not raise any objection relating to his entitlement to be upgraded as Constable Grade I and Head Constable at an earlier point of time by including the LWP, instead continued to discharge his duties accepting the upgradation from the respective dates.

sentences.text: This Court by an order dated 31.08.2018 having directed the respondents to take an informed and considered decision thereon in accordance with law, the respondent issued the impugned endorsement proceedings dated 20.12.2018 which is assailed in the present writ petition.

30. As noted herein above, the petitioner started submitting representations only as late as 2017 and 2018, claiming he ought to have been upgraded as Constable Grade I and Head Constable at an earlier point of time and not on the date on which he was upgraded, knowing very well that the said dates as claimed by him if accepted, would make him eligible for consideration to be upgraded as Special Sub Inspector in the year 2018.
Thus, the petitioner till such time did not record any objection or protest for delaying the upgradation as claimed in the aforesaid representations.

31. The upgradation of the petitioner to the position of Constable Grade I having taken place in the year 2004 and as Head Constable in the year 2009 (i.e) 13 years and 8 years respectively prior to the petitioner https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis ( Uploaded on: 07/11/2025 07:48:40 pm ) submitting his first representation, the same cannot be considered as having been filed immediately when the right of the petitioner was affected for it to be considered as being in time.

32. It is settled position of law in service matters delay and latches play a vital role, even if a Government servant is entitled for being granted benefit if he had not taken any action immediately and slept over his rights, the equity Court can deny granting of relief.

(See : Karnataka Power Corporation Ltd. Vs. Thangappan and another reported in (2006) 4 SCC 322 and Chennai Metropolitan Water Supply & Sewerage Board and others V. T.T. Murali Babu reported in (2014) 4 SCC 108)
33.

sentences.text: In the facts of the present case, the petitioner not only slept over his rights, if any existed, but choose to maintain static silence in asserting his right.

The fact the petitioner was upgraded to Constable Grade I and Head Constable in the year 2004 and 2009 respectively, during which period disciplinary proceedings / appeal proceedings / mercy petition were pending consideration
, it is not difficult to discern the reason for the petitioner's silence regarding his claim for inclusion of LWP period as period of service rendered.

The endeavour of the petitioner in submitting https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis ( Uploaded on: 07/11/2025 07:48:40 pm ) representations from August 2017 onwards thus appears to be only for the purpose of making a claim for being upgraded as Special Sub Inspector.
However, it is to be noted that the upgradation to Special Sub Inspector is not solely on the basis of length of service put in, but is also required to have unblemished record.

Since, by virtue of the proceedings of the first respondent, the petitioner is visited with a Black Mark, it cannot be said that the petitioner has unblemished carrier for him to feel aggrieved by non consideration for upgradation to Special Sub Inspector or he being deprived of the opportunity of upgradation on account of considering wrong date of upgradation as Constable Grade I and Head Constable.

34. Thus, the petitioner having accepted his upgradation to constable Grade I and Head Constable,
cannot merely by submitting representation in the year 2017, approaching this Court and obtaining S.Ramesh Babu vs The Director General Of Police on 7 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/29454605/
7

sentences.text: an order directing the respondents to consider the said representation in accordance with law and on the respondents issuing the impugned proceedings in the form of endorsement cannot approach this Court, claiming that his right having been affected by the impugned proceeding.
It is to be noted that the impugned proceeding not give raise to any new cause of action and the cause of action if any had arisen firstly in the year 2004 and secondly in the year 2009.
https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis
35. Since, the petitioner had accepted his upgradation in the said years (i.e,) 2004 and 2009 respectively, it is not open for the petitioner to raise the said issue after such long lapse of time.

36. The Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Union of India and others V. M.K.Sarkar reported in (2010) 2 SCC 59 dealing with a direction to consider and dispose of the representation and on the basis of the order passed, pursuant to the said direction held as under :-
15.

entities.text: Union of India and others V. M.K.Sarkar reported in (2010) 2 SCC 59
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: When a belated representation in regard to a stale or dead issue/dispute is considered and decided, in compliance with a direction by the court/tribunal to do so, the date of such decision cannot be considered as furnishing a fresh cause of action for reviving the dead issue or time-barred dispute.

The issue of limitation or delay and laches should be considered with reference to the original cause of action and not with reference to the date on which an order is passed in compliance with a court's direction.

Neither a court's direction to consider a representation issued without examining the merits, nor a decision given in compliance with such direction, will extend the limitation, or erase the delay and laches.
https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis

37. Having regard to the law laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of M.K.Sarkar (cited supra), the impugned proceedings being only a reiteration of the stand taken by the respondents while granting upgradation to the petitioner in the year 2004 and 2009 and the petitioner having accepted the said proceedings and having acted thereon, the claim of the petitioner in the present writ petition is to be considered as stale claim, liable to be rejected.
38. Insofar as the cases of this Court on which reliance is placed by the learned counsel for the petitioner are concerned
, it is to be noted that the aforesaid cases did not deal with the issue as to whether LWP is to be included or excluded while counting the period of service.
All the aforesaid cases as pointed out by the learned Special Government Pleader are in relation to promotion and thus would not advance the case of the petitioner.
39. Thus, considered from any angle, this Court is of the view that the present writ petition as filed is devoid of merits and is liable to be dismissed.
https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis ( Uploaded on: 07/11/2025 07:48:40 pm )
40. Accordingly, the Writ Petition is dismissed.
No order as to costs.

The fulcrum of the petitioner's case is that on the order of removal from service being set aside and thereafter the petitioner being visited with penalty of reduction in time scale of pay by three stages for three years with cumulative effect and the said order of punishment being modified in appeal to postponement of increment for one year without cumulative effect and the said order further being modified to a punishment / recording of Black Mark in service register in a mercy petition filed by the petitioner herein, the period of suspension and out of service is to be regularised as per Rule 54 of Tamil Nadu Government Servant Fundamental Rules applicable to the Government servant; and that if the period of suspension and out of service is considered as being in duty, he would be eligible for upgradation as Grade I Constable on 09.06.2003, as Head Constable on 09.06.2008 and https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis ( Uploaded on: 07/11/2025 07:48:40 pm )
further being eligible to be upgraded as Special Sub Inspector on completion of 10 years from 10.06.2018.

It is to be noted that the modification of the punishment initially awarded (i.e,) reduction in time scale of pay by three stages for three years with cumulative effect, to finally one of the punishment of Black Mark by the first respondent vide his proceedings dated 14.03.2011, firstly, cannot be said as if the petitioner is not visited with any punishment and secondly, having been reinstated into service on the ground that the charges has not been proved against him or by giving benefit of doubt or any other technical ground, for him to claim the benefit under Rule 54 of the Fundamental Rules.

opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
Thus, the petitioner till such time did not record any objection or protest for delaying the upgradation as claimed in the aforesaid representations.
31. The upgradation of the petitioner to the position of Constable Grade I having taken place in the year 2004 and as Head Constable in the year 2009 (i.e) 13 years and 8 years respectively prior to the petitioner https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis ( Uploaded on: 07/11/2025 07:48:40 pm ) submitting his first representation, the same cannot be considered as having been filed immediately when the right of the petitioner was affected for it to be considered as being in time.
32. It is settled position of law in service matters delay and latches play a vital role, even if a Government servant is entitled for being granted benefit if he had not taken any action immediately and slept over his rights, the equity Court can deny granting of relief.
(See : Karnataka Power Corporation Ltd. Vs. Thangappan and another reported in (2006) 4 SCC 322 and Chennai Metropolitan Water Supply & Sewerage Board and others V. T.T. Murali Babu reported in (2014) 4 SCC 108)
33.
In the facts of the present case, the petitioner not only slept over his rights, if any existed, but choose to maintain static silence in asserting his right.
The fact the petitioner was upgraded to Constable Grade I and Head Constable in the year 2004 and 2009 respectively, during which period disciplinary proceedings / appeal proceedings / mercy petition were pending consideration
However, it is to be noted that the upgradation to Special Sub Inspector is not solely on the basis of length of service put in, but is also required to have unblemished record.
Since, by virtue of the proceedings of the first respondent, the petitioner is visited with a Black Mark, it cannot be said that the petitioner has unblemished carrier for him to feel aggrieved by non consideration for upgradation to Special Sub Inspector or he being deprived of the opportunity of upgradation on account of considering wrong date of upgradation as Constable Grade I and Head Constable.
34. Thus, the petitioner having accepted his upgradation to constable Grade I and Head Constable,
cannot merely by submitting representation in the year 2017, approaching this Court and obtaining S.Ramesh Babu vs The Director General Of Police on 7 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/29454605/
7
an order directing the respondents to consider the said representation in accordance with law and on the respondents issuing the impugned proceedings in the form of endorsement cannot approach this Court, claiming that his right having been affected by the impugned proceeding.
It is to be noted that the impugned proceeding not give raise to any new cause of action and the cause of action if any had arisen firstly in the year 2004 and secondly in the year 2009.
35. Since, the petitioner had accepted his upgradation in the said years (i.e,) 2004 and 2009 respectively, it is not open for the petitioner to raise the said issue after such long lapse of time.
The issue of limitation or delay and laches should be considered with reference to the original cause of action and not with reference to the date on which an order is passed in compliance with a court's direction.
Neither a court's direction to consider a representation issued without examining the merits, nor a decision given in compliance with such direction, will extend the limitation, or erase the delay and laches.
